findings.evidence: Mathlib/Probability/Moments/Covariance.lean:81 `lemma covariance_const_left [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (c : ℝ) : cov[fun _ ↦ c, Y; μ] = 0` — the vanishing of the covariance of a constant needs normalisation; covariance is `∫ (X - μ[X]) * (Y - μ[Y]) ∂μ`, giving `2 v i v j` for the mass-2 example above.
findings.fix: Replace `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]` by `[IsProbabilityMeasure μ]` in the `IsNoiseModel` section and in `ofRandomVector`/`ofRandomVector_value`/`ofRandomVector_covariance`/`isNoiseModel_ofRandomVector` (the instance implies `IsFiniteMeasure`, so the proofs go through unchanged). In the Mathlib-mirroring file keep `IsFiniteMeasure` but say 'its integral `μ[·]`' rather than 'its mean'.
findings.issue: `IsNoiseModel` requires only `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]` at every use site. For an unnormalised finite measure `μ[X i]` is not a mean, and Mathlib's `cov` of a constant is nonzero, so the structure's own field docstrings ('the means of the components ... are the central values') and the module claim 'the exactly determined functionals are those that carry no noise' are false. Counterexample: `μ = 2·P`, `X ≡ v` constant, `v ≠ 0`. Then `μ[X i] = 2 v i` and `cov[X i, X j; μ] = ∫ (v i - 2 v i)(v j - 2 v j) dμ = 2 v i v j`, so `D.covariance = 2 v vᵀ` and `determinedSubspace = ker (2 v vᵀ) = v^⊥`; `c = v` is not in it although `v ⬝ᵥ X = ‖v‖²` is almost surely constant, i.e. carries no noise. Same weakness in `ofRandomVector` (line 204) and `isNoiseModel_ofRandomVector` (line 225), whose 'central values are the means' holds only after normalisation, and in the prose of `ae_eq_integral_iff_covarianceMatrix_mulVec_eq_zero` (CovarianceMatrix.lean:110), which says 'its mean' for what is `μ[·]`.

findings.evidence: roadmap/EpsilonEridaniRoadmaps/LatticeBridge/README.md:259 'A *Euclidean dataset* is a finite indexed family of observations with a positive semidefinite covariance on the index set'; README.md:135 Convention 10. Mathlib's `PosSemidef` is Finsupp-based (LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean:60), which is why the unbundled version elaborates.
findings.fix: Add `[Finite ι]` to `EuclideanDataset` (and use `Fintype.ofFinite` where a variance is formed), or, if the extra generality is deliberate, drop the 'finitely many' claim from the module docstring and restrict `HasContinuumLimit` to finite label types.
findings.issue: `EuclideanDataset ι` places no finiteness constraint on `ι`, so `EuclideanDataset ℕ` typechecks, while the roadmap defines the object as 'a finite indexed family' (README §0.1) and Convention 10 states 'Euclidean data is finite and carries a covariance'; the file's own docstring (line 15) asserts 'finitely many renormalised matrix elements'. `HasContinuumLimit` (line 117) is likewise stated for arbitrary `ι`, where convergence in the Pi topology is mere pointwise convergence of entries.

summary: The linear algebra and the variance/kernel characterisations are faithful, but `IsNoiseModel` and `ofRandomVector` are stated for an arbitrary finite measure, under which `μ[X i]` is not a mean and a noise-free functional need not lie in the determined subspace, so the advertised reading of the headline theorem fails. The dataset structure also drops the finiteness the roadmap makes definitional.
